# Ryujinx shader translator (vendored subset)

Three projects from Ryujinx 1.3.2: `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader`, `Ryujinx.Common` and `Spv.Generator`, with these local changes:

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs`, `GenerateTextureSample`:
  - Texel offsets that are not constants (Maxwell AOFFI / TLD4.PTP offsets read from a register) are built with `OpCompositeConstruct` and passed as `Offset`. A four-offset gather becomes four one-offset gathers, each giving component w. Upstream wrote them as an `OpConstantComposite` with `ConstOffset(s)`, which is invalid SPIR-V; SPIRV-Cross threw `nullptr` and the shader never built (2026-10-18: 8 shaders in Wonder, Link's Awakening, Tears of the Kingdom and Age of Calamity). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.
  - Texture coordinates that are NaN are replaced by 0 (the `nfZero` select). This came with the first import.
- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Translation/Optimizations/BindlessElimination.cs`, `TryGetOperation` / `IsSameOperand`: a bindless handle that reaches the texture instruction through a phi is followed through the phis that feed it (a handle kept in a loop variable comes back through the loop's own phi), and two `constant buffer | constant` handles count as the same value. Upstream compared only the phi's direct inputs, so such handles fell to the texture-pool array of 32 (`*_t2d_cb0_40000000`), which cannot be bound; 218 pixel shaders in Monster Hunter Rise (2026-10-20). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.
- The same file, `TryTableHandle` and `IsBindlessHandleAllowed`, with `Translation/Optimizations/Optimizer.cs` (a second sweep) and `Translation/ResourceManager.cs` (`GetTextureTypes`): a handle phi that `GenerateBindlessAccess` refuses, because some inputs are not handles (undefined, or values kept in the same register on paths where the predicated read does not run), takes the c2 handles among its inputs. With one, it takes the phi's place; with several, one read per handle, and the result is chosen by comparing the phi's value with each handle at run time. Upstream removed such reads and wrote 0: 58,122 reads in FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (2026-10-26, GitHub issue #168). See [Bindless reads whose handle phi also carries other values](../../../docs/reference/shaders.md#bindless-reads-whose-handle-phi-also-carries-other-values). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Instructions/InstEmitTexture.cs`, `EmitTex` (TLD 1D with integer coordinates only) and `EmitTexs` (TLDS `Texture1DLodZero`), with `IGpuAccessor.RecordTexelFetch1D`: Maxwell reads a 1D texture and a texture buffer with the same instruction, and the bound descriptor decides. When the texture type query does not answer "buffer", the read is translated as 2D at `(x & 0x3FFF, x >> 14)` instead of `(x, 0)`, and the handle is reported. A 1D texture (one row at most 16384 wide on the host) reads the same; the host binds a texture buffer in such a slot as a linear 2D texture of 16384-texel rows over its memory (`nvn_mtl.m` `tbuf_as_2d`). Upstream read `(x, 0)` and the host had only a dummy texture to give: the light and decal lists of Age of Calamity (at least 15,000 shaders) and Three Houses read zeros (2026-10-21). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Translation/EmitterContext.cs` and `Translation/ShaderDefinitions.cs`: fixed-input compute lowering explicitly forwards passthrough positions and all captured generic attributes not replaced by the geometry shader, and inherits its output primitive from input topology. Independent offline stages have no next-stage usage mask, and Metal cannot provide the native NV passthrough raster stage. See [passthrough compute emission](../../../docs/reference/shaders.md#passthrough-geometry-kernels-lose-raster-vertices) and [output bounds](../../../docs/reference/shaders.md#passthrough-geometry-output-bounds-follow-input-topology).

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Instructions/InstEmitSurface.cs`, `IntermediateRepresentation/TextureFlags.cs` and `CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs`: the Metal path (`TranslationFlags.MetalImageAtomics`) bounds image atomics before forming the texel pointer, which SPIRV-Cross writes as a native texture atomic (MSL 3.1) on buffer, 2D, 2D-array and 3D images. Returning `IGN` atomics preserve the old texel on the valid edge and return zero outside the image; CAS is a native texture compare-exchange behind the same guard; predicate results and non-IGN modes remain rejected. See [bounds of image atomics](../../../docs/reference/shaders.md#bounds-of-image-atomics) and [image atomics](../../../docs/reference/shaders.md#image-atomics), found on SHIN MEGAMI TENSEI V: Vengeance's particle counters.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Instructions/InstEmitAmpereAlu.cs` (`AShfl`), `IntermediateRepresentation/Instruction.cs`, `StructuredIr/InstructionInfo.cs`, `Translation/EmitterContextInsts.cs` and `CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs`: a pixel shader's SHFL inside its 2x2 quad (immediate lane, immediate mask 0x1c03) becomes `OpGroupNonUniformQuadBroadcast` (IDX, lane 0..3) or `OpGroupNonUniformQuadSwap` (BFLY 1..3), with a true predicate. Upstream wrote a plain subgroup shuffle, which on Adreno may leave out a helper pixel (garbage) or pair lanes that are not the quad's. As the Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave Eden build does (`dm/third_party/eden-fefw`, `frontend/ampere/ops_memory.cpp`) and Lemon 167eb5934b37 (Adreno streaks). 488 of Fortune's Weave's pixel shaders, all BFLY (2026-11-09). `XLATE_NO_QUAD=1` turns it off. Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/StructuredIr/AstOptimizer.cs`, `Optimize`: a variable passed to a call is not propagated. SPIR-V passes call arguments by pointer (StructuredProgram copies each to a temporary); propagated, the call held a constant or an expression and the temporary was removed, and translation failed with `KeyNotFoundException` in `CodeGenContext.GetLocalPointer`. Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave: the 459 shaders that only translated with the optimizer off (debug mode) now translate optimized, 39% fewer instructions (2026-11-09). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.
- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Instructions/InstEmitAmpereTensor.cs` (`AShuffle`; REDUX, MATCH, HMMA, LDSM, MOVM): shuffles go to a lane of the thread's own 32-lane warp and the active lanes are that warp's ballot word, when the host subgroup is wider than 32 (`QueryHostSubgroupSize`, the Android chain's 128). Written for Metal's 32-wide SIMD groups, warps past the first used the first warp's values on Adreno: Fortune's Weave's tile depth bounds (REDUX min / max / sum in `a0c632d8b5fa925b`). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/StructuredIr/AstOptimizer.cs`, `Optimize` / `WritesMemory`: an assignment whose source writes memory (an atomic, an image atomic) is neither removed when its result is unused nor moved to its single use. Upstream removed it, and the write with it: Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave's light culling (`35d12d6f98fa05e2`, 11 atomic ORs) and `d5bc99ffd183fa20` (8) never wrote their results in the optimized translation, and its exposure histogram (`6d0f6db3f0d396a3`, 5 atomic adds) stayed empty once it translated optimized (the picture came out dark). As shirai91/nx2android 44eca7e671. Checked by running the translations on a PC GPU with the same inputs (the work folder's `re/csrun`: 120 runs, the optimized 64-lane translation against the unoptimized 32-lane one, identical; 2026-11-10). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.
- `Translation/EmitterContextInsts.cs` (`WarpGather`, `SubgroupBroadcast`), `Translation/HelperFunctionManager.cs` (the four shuffle helpers), `Instructions/InstEmitAmpereTensor.cs` (`AShuffle`), `IntermediateRepresentation/Instruction.cs`, `StructuredIr/InstructionInfo.cs`, `CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs`: on a host subgroup wider than the 32-lane warp, a lane of the thread's own warp is read with `OpGroupNonUniformBroadcast` (a constant lane), one per warp of the subgroup, chosen by the thread's lane id. A shuffle with a computed lane (the warp's first lane + the lane) is what this replaces: Qualcomm's driver does not run those right (Eden's `has_broken_spirv_subgroup_shuffle`), and Fortune's Weave's seven warp compute shaders came out wrong with them. At 32 lanes (Metal) the plain shuffle is unchanged. The Android chain answers 64 lanes (`vk_spirv.py` `SUBGROUP`). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Instructions/InstEmitAmpereTensor.cs` (`ARedux`), `Translation/EmitterContextInsts.cs` (`SubgroupReduce`), `IntermediateRepresentation/Instruction.cs`, `StructuredIr/InstructionInfo.cs`, `CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs` (`GenerateSubgroupReduce`): on a host subgroup of several warps, REDUX is one subgroup reduction per warp (`OpGroupNonUniformBitwiseAnd` / `Or` / `Xor` / `IAdd` / `SMin` / `SMax` / `UMin` / `UMax`; the other warps' lanes give the identity), not 32 broadcasts and selects per warp. Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave's light culling (`35d12d6f98fa05e2`) went from 10,387 to 2,887 SPIR-V lines; the per-lane form ran 150-212 ms a dispatch on the Odin 3 (Adreno 830) and lost the device. Needs `VK_SUBGROUP_FEATURE_ARITHMETIC_BIT`. Marked `nxnative:` in the code.
- `StructuredIr/AstOptimizer.cs`, `HasSubgroupOp`: an assignment whose source holds a subgroup operation (ballot, shuffle, vote, broadcast, reduction, quad) is not propagated to its use, which may sit in a branch or loop where other lanes are active. With the reductions above propagated, 31 of 120 PC runs differed from the unoptimized translation; with this, none (the work folder's `re/csrun`, 2026-11-10). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

The shader translation tool in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate` references them to translate the original Switch shaders to SPIR-V.
